regressionChecked: Critical fix re-verified by direct code read: meeting-deletion.service.ts:35-36 now takes EntityResolver.lockUserGraph before meetings.lockOwned, matching every other graph writer's lock order; no other transaction acquires the meetings row lock before the graph lock, so this ordering introduces no new deadlock potential

New deterministic e2e (graph.e2e.spec.ts:263-289) proves the fix under real concurrency: holds the graph lock in a second pg connection, confirms the DELETE is still pending after 400ms, inserts a new mention for the entity, commits, then confirms the DELETE completes and the entity survives with mention_count 1 (not deleted) — this is the exact race described in the prior critical finding, closed

findings.summary: (Prior finding, now fixed) Meeting deletion did not hold the per-user graph advisory lock, so it could race a concurrent resolve/merge/edit and delete an entity that had just gained a legitimate new mention. Fixed by taking EntityResolver.lockUserGraph as the transaction's first statement, before the meeting row lock. Verified by a new deterministic e2e that blocks the DELETE on a held lock, inserts a mention, commits, and confirms the entity survives (graph.e2e.spec.ts:263-289).
(Prior finding, now fixed) meetingGraph's node query lacked an explicit user_id filter, relying on an unstated invariant. Fixed: query now carries 'AND e.user_id = $2', matching the edges query.

(Prior finding, now fixed) A merge suggestion between entities that no longer share a type (after a later PATCH edit) could still surface. Fixed: suggestions query now requires 'a.type = b.type' at read time.

Independently found and fixed during rework (not from my prior review): a search string with no letters or digits (e.g. '%', punctuation only) normalized to the empty string, which then matched every entity via 'LIKE %%'  — effectively an unintended wildcard-everything search. Now short-circuits to an empty page. Covered by graph.e2e.spec.ts:178-181.

The relation-matching find() re-normalizes each candidate entity's name per call instead of reusing the 'known' map already built during entity parsing. No correctness issue, minor dedup opportunity. Not addressed in this round; still deferred.
